newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Rugby Union - Zinny braced for the battle of Albany.
newsitem.headline: Rugby Union - Zinny braced for the battle of Albany.

text.p: AUCKLAND, March 14 - Auckland Blues captain Zinzan Brooke, playing in his first Super 12 rugby game of the season tonight, is braced for a fierce encounter against the Waikato Chiefs at Albany, NZPA reports.
A leg injury kept Brooke out of the Blues' two opening matches in South Africa, against Northern Transvaal and Orange Free State.
Neither game, however, is expected to match the intensity of what the Blues will face tonight at the Chiefs' new ground, just north of Auckland.
"It is going to be difficult because they (Waikato) are on a high. They're in a better position than they were last year when they'd lost a couple of early games," Brooke said.
"They have a lot experience up front so they are going to be hard to knock over.
"We have to make sure that we get an edge there (in the forwards) because I know they've got the backs to fire a few shots."
Brooke singled out veteran prop Richard Loe, captain and lock Ian Jones, and Counties captain and former Blues player Errol Brain as men Auckland would have to keep an eye on.
"In having Richard Loe and Ian Jones they have two key players, and then they have guys like Errol Brain who was with the Blues last year," Brooke said.
"Errol's been playing very, very well so it is going to be a tight tussle."
His major concern for the team was the way they let their minds wander from the job in the second game in South Africa.
"Against Orange Free State the concentration lapsed in a few stages and it was unusual to see some of the experienced guys making a few mistakes," he said.

"I don't know what to put it down to, maybe the guys had a foot on the plane, or it (a poorer performance) was due, but there were too many mistakes for my liking and I don't want that to happen against the Chiefs."
Brooke spoke for the squad when he said that coming back from South Africa and having to re-adjust to New Zealand time had made it tough for the players.
"It was hard coming back from South Africa and getting into the training sessions, so it is all up top now," he said.
The match kicks off at 7.30 p.m.

Auckland Blues: Carlos Spencer, Jeremy Stanley, Eroni Clarke, Joeli Vidiri, Tony Marsh, Lee Stensness, Ofisa Tonu'u, Zinzan Brooke (capt), Mark Carter, Richard Fromont, Robin Brooke, Michael Jones, Olo Brown, Sean Fitzpatrick, Craig Dowd. Reserves: Norm Berryman, Michael Scott, Dean Sheppard, Andrew Roose, Paul Thomson, Dylan Mika.

Waikato Chiefs: Matthew Cooper, Bruce Reihana, Frank Bunce, Scott McLeod, Walter Little, Ian Foster, Mark Robinson, Errol Brain, Dean Anglesey, Glenn Taylor, Ian Jones (captain), Blair Larsen, Richard Loe, Greg Smith, Michael Collins. Reserves: Rhys Duggan, Blair Feeney, Deon Matthews, Lee Lidgard, Paul Mitchell, Brett Sinkinson.
